question: A 45-year-old woman diagnosed with stage IV breast cancer with multiple bone metastases, undergoing hormonal treatment and intravenous bisphosphonates. He comes to his office referring to intense basal bone pain (EVA = 7), in several locations, without associated neurological symptoms and pain exacerbations (EVA = 9) several times a day that force him to remain at rest. On treatment with ibuprofen (600 mg every 8 hours) and tramadol (150 mg daily). What treatment would you consider more appropriate in this patient to improve pain control?

options.opa: Suspend ibuprofen and tramadol and start a major opioid such as morphine or oxycodone.
options.opb: Stop tramadol, maintain ibuprofen and start a major opioid such as morphine or oxycodone.
options.opc: Suspend ibuprofen and tramadol and start a major opioid such as morphine or oxycodone, and at the same time treatment for breakthrough pain with sublingual fentanyl.
options.opd: Suspend tramadol, maintain ibuprofen and initiate a major opioid such as morphine or oxycodone, and at the same time treatment for breakthrough pain with sublingual fentanyl.
